s1.syndrome_frame: Recurrent vaginal bleeding with intermittent vaginal mass sensation and abnormal vaginal discharge
salient_findings: Vaginal bleeding with clots every 1-2 weeks
Watery, nonfoul-smelling vaginal discharge between bleeding episodes
Firm, globular 6x4 cm mass within the vaginal canal
key_facts: 15-month history of vaginal bleeding
Intermittent sensation of a mass in the vagina
Bleeding with clots every 1-2 weeks lasting 2-5 days
Watery, nonfoul-smelling vaginal discharge between bleeding episodes
Occasional postcoital bleeding
Denies dyspnea, palpitations, or bleeding from other sites
Three home vaginal deliveries
Minilaparotomy sterilization 11 years prior
Tubal recanalization 5 years ago
Prior evaluations did not alleviate symptoms
Hemoglobin 5.3 g/dL with normal platelet count and PT/INR
Pelvic ultrasonography reported as normal
Firm, globular 6x4 cm mass within the vaginal canal on examination

shortlist.label: Vaginal leiomyoma
shortlist.why_kept: Firm, globular mass within the vaginal canal and history of vaginal bleeding

shortlist.label: Uterine leiomyoma
shortlist.why_kept: History of vaginal bleeding and prior evaluations did not alleviate symptoms

shortlist.label: Cervical cancer
shortlist.why_kept: Abnormal vaginal bleeding and presence of a mass

shortlist.label: Vaginal cancer
shortlist.why_kept: Vaginal bleeding and presence of a mass in the vaginal canal

shortlist.label: Aggressive angiomyxoma
shortlist.why_kept: Intermittent sensation of a mass in the vagina and watery vaginal discharge

raw.rationale: The presence of a firm, globular 6x4 cm mass within the vaginal canal, along with a 15-month history of vaginal bleeding and intermittent sensation of a mass, is most consistent with a vaginal leiomyoma, which is a rare benign tumor that can cause bleeding and a palpable mass.

rejected.label: Uterine leiomyoma
rejected.why: The mass is described as being within the vaginal canal, and the uterine fundus was not palpable, making uterine leiomyoma less likely

rejected.label: Cervical cancer
rejected.why: There is no mention of abnormal Pap smear results or other risk factors for cervical cancer, and the mass is described as a firm, globular mass rather than an ulcerative lesion

rejected.label: Vaginal cancer
rejected.why: Vaginal cancer is rare and typically presents with more advanced symptoms, such as pelvic pain or urinary symptoms, which are not mentioned in the vignette

rejected.label: Aggressive angiomyxoma
rejected.why: While aggressive angiomyxoma is a rare tumor that can occur in the vagina, it is typically characterized by a soft, gelatinous mass rather than a firm, globular mass
